facts: The paper 'Partisan responsiveness in real time: causal evidence from Trump’s military attack on Iran' is authored by Stuart J. Turnbull-Dugarte, Peter Luca Versteegen, Daniel Devine, and Owen Winter.
The study was published on 2026-11-03 in Political Science Research and Methods (DOI: 10.1017/psrm.2026.10135).
The research investigates whether elite cue effects on partisan public opinion occur in real time.

The authors used a quasi-experimental design leveraging minute-level variation in exposure to President Trump’s unexpected announcement of US military strikes against Iran during a nationally representative survey.
The study found that partisan divergence emerged almost immediately: support for military intervention increased among Republicans but declined among Democrats.
The findings proved robust across 28,672 model specifications and 57,344 partisan-specific treatment effects.
The authors conclude that elite cues can polarize public opinion within minutes, even before media framing and partisan commentary have diffused, carrying implications for democratic accountability.
